observational-unit.def: One individual that data describe, such as a person, an animal, an object or a day. Each row of a data table is one observational unit.

variable.def: A characteristic recorded for each observational unit, whose value can differ from one unit to another.

categorical-variable.def: A variable whose values place each unit in a group or category, such as eye color or yes and no. Numbers used as labels, like ZIP codes, are categorical.

quantitative-variable.def: A variable whose values are numbers that measure or count an amount, so arithmetic with them makes sense.

discrete-variable.def: A quantitative variable that takes separate values with gaps between them, usually a count.

continuous-variable.def: A quantitative variable that can take any value in an interval, usually a measurement such as time, length or weight.

parameter.def: A number that describes a population. It is usually unknown, because finding it needs data on every individual.

statistic.def: A number that describes a sample. It changes from sample to sample and is used to estimate a parameter.

distribution.def: The values a variable takes and how often it takes each value or range of values.
